name:        useInputStatusIcon
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Builds the on-field status affordance for a bordered input and its accessibility wiring, so every input in the family behaves the same for a given status. The attached variant renders a plain glyph and leaves the text to the message box; the detached variant renders nothing here, because the message box already carries its own icon; the tooltip variant renders a real focusable button whose tooltip is reachable by keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive tech. Use it when building a bordered input, not for field-level messaging.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useInputStatusIcon

name:        useTableRowExpansion
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which expands a full-width detail panel below a row, rendered by the consumer via renderExpanded(item). Adds a leading chevron column and a right-click "Expand/Collapse row" action; the consumer owns the expandedKeys set. The panel spans the row but starts its content at the first column, past the chevron, so detail lines up with the labels above it; the inset follows the table density. Use it for master-detail rows (order details, forms, charts, nested tables). For hierarchical data where child rows reuse the parent columns, use useTableTreeData + useTableTreeState instead.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableRowExpansion

name:        useAnnounce
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useAnnounce

name:        useCalendarConstraints
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Calendar
description: Provides date constraint validation for calendar views and custom range pickers. It combines boundary dates, span limits measured from an in-progress range start, and custom rules (such as weekly closures or blackout dates) into an isDateDisabled predicate. Calendar uses it internally to disable day buttons; use it directly when building bespoke scheduling interfaces or range pickers.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useCalendarConstraints

name:        useInputContainer
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Makes an input container wrapper clickable, delegating focus to the inner input/textarea when the user clicks non-interactive areas (icons, padding, status indicators). Built on top of useClickableContainer, so nested interactive elements (clear buttons, calendar toggles, links) are handled safely; clicking them does NOT steal focus from the input. Automatically detects input type: text-like inputs receive .focus(), while other types (checkbox, radio, file) receive .click().
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useInputContainer
